manifest.name: Elecrow CrowPanel 5.79" E-Paper
manifest.description: Elecrow CrowPanel ESP32-S3 5.79 inch black/white e-paper HMI display (792x272, two cascaded SSD1683 controllers). Runs the native Tesserae device firmware (env `elecrow-crowpanel-579`) over the v1 REST device API and paints a raw 1-bpp mono buffer (26928 bytes) produced by the esp32_bw_bin renderer. The rotary switch moves through the rotation and its press re-renders; microSD slot supported; no battery sense on this board.
manifest.notes_md:
Awaiting confirmed test on real hardware. Wire format is exactly 26928 bytes (792*272/8), MSB=leftmost pixel, bit-set=white, bit-clear=black; no header, no padding, no checksum. The two controllers each drive 396 columns and leave an 8-column seam in their shared RAM; the firmware inserts it, so the frame carries only visible pixels. Default device ids look like CrowPanel_579_<mac-suffix>.

**Colour depth.** Mono is the default. Firmware that advertises `"gamuts": ["mono", "gray_4"]` in its register and status bodies can also paint a 4-level grey frame from `esp32_gray2_bin`: exactly 53856 bytes (792*272/4, 198 bytes per row, no row padding), 4 px/byte MSB first, `0b00` black to `0b11` white. The firmware tells the two apart by byte length (26928 mono, 53856 grey), keeps the same kind, model and device id, and only firmware that advertises `gray_4` gets a grey frame, whatever the device card says. Older firmware omits the key and stays on mono. Pick the depth on the device card (Rendering, Colour depth). The grey path is UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE and needs a firmware build that advertises `gamuts`. Relay-paired panels do not advertise it and stay mono.

manifest.name: epdiy v7 + ED133UT2 13.3"
manifest.description: The open-hardware epdiy v7 driver board (ESP32-S3, TPS65185 panel power) with an ED133UT2 13.3 inch panel, 1600x1200 at 16 grey levels. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API; esp32_gray_bin packs a raw 4-bpp linear greyscale buffer (960000 bytes) that the firmware drives onto the panel's parallel bus.
manifest.notes_md:
**UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE.** Firmware support is the `epdiy-v7-ed133ut2` build in tesserae-device-firmware; flash `epdiy-v7-ed133ut2-selftest` first. It paints a lettered, scrambled sheet of the 16 grey levels, then the same bars in order with black at the left, and the serial log names the letter order a tuned matrix gives.

Wire format is exactly 960000 bytes (1600*1200/2), row-major, top-left origin; high nibble = left pixel, 0x0 = black, 0xF = white. The same shape as the PaperS3 and the reTerminal E1003, at a larger size.

The firmware drives the panel with the same parallel driver as the PaperS3, a port of bitbank2's FastEPD, with the v7's TPS65185 power path and gate timing from FastEPD. The grey matrix and VCOM (-2.28 V) are the ED133UT2 tuning from bitbank2/FastEPD#44. Greyscale tuning is a table in the board header, and a panel whose flex cable gives a different VCOM is a one-line change.

No partial refresh yet. No battery, buttons or touch.

manifest.name: Good Display ESP32-133C02 (13.3")
manifest.description: Good Display ESP32-133C02 controller board for the 13.3 inch GDEP133C02 Spectra 6 panel. ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 with 16 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM, 1200x1600 portrait-native dual-controller glass, optional Ref2 buttons SW2/SW3/SW4, and an onboard microSD slot on a separate SPI bus. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API through the tesserae-device-firmware build env `gooddisplay-esp32-133c02`; server-side pack via esp32_bin produces the same 960000-byte 4-bpp Spectra 6 frame used by the Seeed EE02/E1004 targets.
manifest.notes_md: Tested on physical Good Display ESP32-133C02 hardware with the matching tesserae-device-firmware env `gooddisplay-esp32-133c02` and board header `boards/gooddisplay_esp32_133c02.h`. Uses the T133A01/GDEP133C02 dual-controller driver shared with Seeed E1004/EE02 and the pin map from philippwaller/esphome-epaper-spectra6-133. Wire format is exactly 960000 bytes (1200*1600/2), two pixels per byte with high nibble = LEFT/even column and low nibble = RIGHT/odd column, row-major, 600 bytes per row, top-left origin. Palette nibbles match Tesserae's Spectra 6 constants (black=0x0, white=0x1, yellow=0x2, red=0x3, blue=0x5, green=0x6; 0x4 and 0x7 reserved). Ref2 buttons SW2/SW3/SW4 are wired as active-high GPIO12/13/14 and mapped to refresh/left/right; Ref1 boards simply leave those pins unused. The onboard microSD slot is on dedicated SPI pins (CLK=8, MOSI=3, MISO=5, CS=15). GPIO45 is the active-high panel power enable and a strapping pin, so external circuitry must not force it low during boot.

manifest.name: M5Stack M5Paper
manifest.description: 4.7 inch touch ePaper handheld with 16-level greyscale, the original ESP32-D0WDQ6-V3 (classic dual-core, external PSRAM), IT8951 e-paper controller over SPI, 1150 mAh battery, 960x540 native landscape scan mounted portrait. The pre-S3 sibling of the M5Stack PaperS3: same 4.7" ED047TC1 glass, but an IT8951 timing controller sits between the MCU and the panel instead of a raw parallel bus. Pairs with the tesserae-device-firmware ESP-IDF build (unified firmware) and speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API. Server-side pack via esp32_gray_bin produces a raw 4-bpp linear greyscale buffer (259200 bytes) the firmware streams straight into the IT8951's image buffer.

panel.name: 4.7 inch ePaper (16-level greyscale, IT8951 controller, 960x540 scan, portrait mount)

touch_enabled.label: Touch input
touch_enabled.help: Dispatch taps against the dashboard's touch regions. On the M5Paper this needs Stay awake on: the classic ESP32 cannot wake from deep sleep on the touch controller, so a tap only registers while the panel is already awake and polling.

touch_linger_s.label: Touch linger
touch_linger_s.help: Seconds to stay awake after a touch so follow-up taps skip the deep-sleep wake latency. Ignored while Stay awake is on (the panel never sleeps). Only applies when touch input is enabled.

manifest.notes_md:
**Verified end-to-end on hardware 2026-09-10** running tesserae-device-firmware (env `m5stack-m5paper`): a live dashboard frame over the v1 REST device API (readable, unmirrored, upright at the server's default rotation), battery telemetry, the three side buttons, the SHT30 sensor, and GT911 touch dispatch. Pin map from M5Stack's M5GFX / M5Unified / M5EPD, cross-checked. Flash `m5stack-m5paper-selftest` first for a driver-only grey ramp when bringing up a new unit.

**This is the original M5Paper (SKU K097 / v1.1), not the PaperS3.** The classic ESP32-D0WDQ6-V3 reaches the same 4.7" ED047TC1 glass through an **IT8951 controller over SPI**, where the PaperS3 (`m5stack_papers3`) is an ESP32-S3 that bit-bangs the bare panel. Same glass, same 259200-byte wire format, different everything in between. The two SKUs also report the same relay model (`esp32_client`), gamut (`gray_16`) and 960x540 scan at pairing, so nothing on the relay wire tells them apart -- hence `auto_select: false`: relay pairing never infers this kind, an ambiguous report stays on `m5stack_papers3`, and an M5Paper is pinned here by the operator or by the firmware declaring `TESSERAE_DEVICE_KIND`.

Wire format: exactly 259200 bytes (960*540/2), row-major, top-left origin, no mirror. Per byte, high nibble = LEFT pixel, low nibble = RIGHT; 0x0 = black, 0xF = white, linear 16-level greyscale. Identical in shape to `seeed_reterminal_e1003` and `m5stack_papers3`, so this panel needs no new renderer or packer. The ED047TC1 is not left-right mirrored (unlike the E1003's ED103TC2), so the firmware streams rows straight through.

**Composition is 540x960 portrait while `native_w`/`native_h` are 960x540** -- those are the row stride the firmware reads. The firmware does not transpose, so `esp32_gray_bin` rotates the portrait composition 90 degrees CW and packs 480-byte landscape rows.

The GT911 digitiser reports in the 540x960 composition space (the firmware maps its 90-degree-rotated axes onto it), so a tap hit-tests directly against the dashboard's regions. `touch_enabled` is off by default and needs Stay awake: the classic ESP32 can't wake from deep sleep on the touch INT (the same ext1 limit that caps the side buttons), so a tap only registers while the panel is awake and polling. The on-board SHT30 fills `temperature_c` / `humidity_pct` each heartbeat; the BM8563 RTC stays unused. Deep-sleep touch/button wake and the microSD deck cache are the remaining follow-ups.

manifest.name: M5Stack PaperMono
manifest.description: 3.97 inch touch ePaper handheld with 4-level greyscale, ESP32-S3R8 with 8 MB PSRAM, 1150 mAh battery, frontlight, microSD, and on the Pro variant LoRa and NFC; the Lite is the same board without the radios and shares this kind. The SSD1677 controller scans 800x480 landscape and the glass is mounted portrait, but the firmware transposes on the device, so the server composes AND packs ordinary 480x800 portrait: 120-byte rows, no server-side rotation. Pairs with the tesserae-device-firmware build that declares this kind at register, and speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API. Server-side pack via esp32_gray2_bin produces a raw 2-bpp 4-level greyscale buffer (96000 bytes) the firmware paints without any on-device decode.
manifest.notes_md:
**Verified on real hardware 2026-09-12** running tesserae-device-firmware (env `m5stack-papermono`): the four-grey selftest ramp, the captive portal, discover and register, and a live 480x800 dashboard frame over the v1 REST device API (upright, unmirrored, correct greys), plus battery telemetry from the M5PM1 PMIC. The panel is the reTerminal Sticky's controller family (SSD1677, 800x480 scan, portrait mount) so the driver and the wire format carry over; the first pass painted static until the firmware selected this glass's own four-grey OTP waveform, and its panel reset and 3.3 V enable are outputs of an M5IOE1 I2C expander rather than MCU GPIOs. Flash the `m5stack-papermono-selftest` build first on a new unit: four grey bands, black at the top, white at the bottom, with a white square top-left.

Wire format is exactly 96000 bytes, 4 pixels per byte MSB first (bits 7-6 = leftmost pixel), 2-bit value 0b00 = black, 0b11 = white, linear 4-level grey; no header, no padding, no checksum. **`native_w`/`native_h` are 480x800, matching the composition, not the controller's 800x480 scan**: these fields mean the row stride the *firmware* reads, and this firmware transposes on the device like the Sticky's. `orientation` is `portrait`, confirmed on the unit: the selftest's corner wedge painted top-left with black first.

**Pro and Lite share this kind.** The PaperMono Lite drops the SX1262 LoRa radio and the ST25R3916 NFC reader and is otherwise the same board, and this firmware drives neither radio, so one image and one OTA lineage cover both.

Wired on the device: the two side keys (previous / next dashboard, both wake the panel from deep sleep), the buzzer (the `beep_*` settings below), battery telemetry via the PMIC; both keys repaint the panel on the bench, the buzzer is wired but not yet exercised. Not wired yet: the FT6336G touch controller (a different register map from the Goodix driver the other touch panels use), the expander-gated microSD slot for the deck cache, the frontlight, and the RGB LED, so `touch` is false and there is no overlay support until the partial-refresh path is confirmed on this glass.

`auto_select: false` because this SKU is indistinguishable on the wire from `seeed_reterminal_sticky` and `xteink_x4_gray`: same protocol, same gamut, same 480x800 geometry, same 96000 bytes. A device running this firmware names its own kind at register and discover, so nothing is lost there, but relay pairing infers a SKU from the wire signature, and this id sorts ahead of both siblings in that tie-break. Without this flag a Sticky or an X4 pairing over a relay would be relabelled a PaperMono and pinned to the wrong OTA lineage.

touch_enabled.label: Touch input
touch_enabled.help: Wake on touch and dispatch taps/swipes against the dashboard's touch regions. Keeps the touch controller powered through deep sleep (its own low-power monitor mode, a fraction of a milliamp), so battery life shortens a little; the panel stays on battery-friendly full sleep with it off.

touch_linger_s.label: Touch linger
touch_linger_s.help: Seconds to stay awake after a touch interaction so follow-up taps skip the deep-sleep wake latency (boot + WiFi). 0 sleeps immediately. Only applies while touch input is enabled.

frontlight_pct.label: Frontlight
frontlight_pct.help: Brightness of the panel's built-in frontlight, as a percentage. 0 is off. The power-management chip keeps the light running while the panel sleeps, so a lit panel is a steady draw on the battery (M5Stack measures roughly 30 mA at 50 percent); best on USB power.

beep_enabled.label: Beep on interaction
beep_enabled.help: Sound the on-board buzzer the moment a button press registers, before the server is contacted. E-ink takes seconds to repaint, so without it there is no confirmation the panel heard you. Off by default: a panel that starts beeping unannounced is worse than a silent one.

beep_tone.label: Beep tone
beep_tone.help: Which sound to make. The server sends the actual notes, so these are editable without a firmware update. The buzzer is a passive piezo, loudest around 2 kHz.

beep_pattern.label: Custom tone
beep_pattern.help: Only used when the tone is set to Custom. Notes as frequency:milliseconds pairs, comma separated, e.g. 1800:30,2600:40. A frequency of 0 is a rest. Up to 8 notes, 200-8000 Hz, 1 second total.

beep_volume.label: Beep volume
beep_volume.help: Drive strength as a percentage. The piezo is loudest at 100 and audible but discreet around 30; 0 is silent, same as turning the beep off.

manifest.name: M5Stack PaperS3
manifest.description: 4.7 inch touch ePaper handheld with 16-level greyscale, ESP32-S3R8 with 8 MB PSRAM, 1800 mAh battery, 960x540 native landscape scan mounted portrait. Pairs with the tesserae-device-firmware ESP-IDF build (unified firmware) and speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API. Server-side pack via esp32_gray_bin produces a raw 4-bpp linear greyscale buffer (259200 bytes) the firmware drives straight onto the panel's parallel bus.

panel.name: 4.7 inch ePaper (16-level greyscale, 960x540 scan, portrait mount)

manifest.notes_md:
**UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE.** Added from issue #21 on tesserae-device-firmware, against the reporter's working pin map and bitbank2 FastEPD's `BB_PANEL_M5PAPERS3` definition. Flash the `m5stack-papers3-selftest` firmware target first and judge the 16 grey bands before pointing a real dashboard at it.

Wire format is exactly 259200 bytes (960*540/2), row-major, top-left origin, no mirror. Per byte: high nibble = LEFT pixel, low nibble = RIGHT pixel; nibble value 0x0 = black, 0xF = white, linear 16-level greyscale. Identical in shape to `seeed_reterminal_e1003`, which is why this panel needed no new renderer or packer -- only this entry.

**Composition is 540x960 portrait while `native_w`/`native_h` are 960x540.** Those fields mean the row stride the *firmware* reads, and this firmware does not transpose: the panel's source driver scans 960 across, so `esp32_gray_bin` rotates the portrait composition 90 degrees CW and packs 240-byte landscape rows. Portrait is the composition because the device is a portrait handheld -- the body is 121.5 x 67.7 mm and the 4.7" 16:9 glass puts its 960-pixel axis along the long side. Byte count alone does not validate this: a landscape composition packs to the same 259200 bytes and paints sideways.

**The 90-degree direction is a guess, not a measurement.** Nothing here has been on real glass, so if the first frame lands upside down, set the display's `flip` and the pair is correct; that is the expected correction and it needs no code change.

This is the first panel Tesserae drives with no controller chip in between. The firmware's `parallel_epd_gray` driver (Family F) shifts 2-bit drive codes into the panel's source driver over the ESP32-S3's LCD/i80 bus and clocks the gate driver by hand, with the 16 greys coming from a per-level pass matrix rather than a controller's waveform flash. Consequences worth knowing: greyscale tuning is a table in the board header rather than a vendor LUT, and there is no partial refresh yet, so this SKU does not offer overlay tap-echo or touch-v3.

The GT911 digitiser is present on the hardware but `touch` is false: this board routes no touch-reset line to the MCU, and the firmware's GT911 driver needs one to pin the controller's I2C address. Touch is a follow-up, sequenced after the panel deliberately -- a display that paints correctly is the prerequisite for any touch result being meaningful.

manifest.name: paperlesspaper OpenPaper 7
manifest.description: 7.3 inch 6-colour Spectra 6 ePaper picture frame from paperlesspaper (Germany), open hardware: ESP32-C6 (4 MB flash, no PSRAM), 4 x AAA NiMH cells, CP2102N USB-C serial. 800x480 landscape-native panel, single controller, composed portrait (480x800) by default since the frame stands upright; the renderer rotates onto the native stride at pack time. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API and paints a 4-bpp Spectra 6 buffer (192000 bytes) produced by the esp32_bin renderer. Pair with the tesserae-device-firmware ESP-IDF build (env paperlesspaper-openpaper-7, boards/paperlesspaper_openpaper_7.h).

panel.name: 7.3 inch Spectra 6 ePaper (800x480 native, portrait mount)

manifest.notes_md: Confirmed on real hardware running tesserae-device-firmware (2026-09-09). Runs the Tesserae firmware in place of the vendor's cloud firmware. Flashing it overwrites the SPIFFS region that holds the frame's paperlesspaper cloud certificate; paperlesspaper support can provision a new one for a frame that wants the vendor cloud back, or read the region first (`esptool.py --chip esp32c6 read_flash 0x3B0000 0x40000 openpaper-spiffs.bin`) to keep your own copy. The board carries a 16 MB NAND flash and a MEMS orientation sensor; Tesserae uses neither yet. Palette nibbles match the firmware's EPD_COL_* constants byte-for-byte (black=0x0, white=0x1, yellow=0x2, red=0x3, blue=0x5, green=0x6). The big button is a hardware reset, which the firmware treats as a wake-and-repaint; the small one is the BOOT button for flashing. The vendor calibrates the battery divider at roughly 2.83:1 across board revisions; Tesserae's reading has not been checked against a meter yet, so treat the reported voltage as approximate. Composition is 480x800 portrait while `native_w`/`native_h` stay 800x480: the firmware reads 400-byte landscape rows and does not transpose, so `esp32_bin` rotates the portrait composition 90 degrees CW on pack, the same arrangement as the M5Paper S3 and Xteink X4 entries. `portrait` is confirmed on a production unit (2026-09-09): a marked test frame painted with its top band at the top of the glass and the USB-C port at the bottom, which is how the frame stands. A unit that somehow paints the other way round takes `portrait_flipped` in Settings -> Devices without any code change.

manifest.name: paperlesspaper OpenPaper L
manifest.description: 13.3 inch 6-colour Spectra 6 ePaper picture frame from paperlesspaper (Germany): ESP32-C6 (4 MB flash, no PSRAM), 4 x AA NiMH cells, CP2102N USB-C serial. 1200x1600 portrait-native E Ink EL133UF3 panel on two controllers. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API; the esp32_bin renderer packs the same 4-bpp 960000-byte frame as the Waveshare 13.3E6, which the firmware streams into the panel controllers in row blocks because it cannot hold the frame in RAM. Pair with the tesserae-device-firmware ESP-IDF build (env paperlesspaper-openpaper-l, boards/paperlesspaper_openpaper_l.h).
manifest.notes_md: Not yet confirmed on real hardware: the firmware target was written from the vendor's open firmware without an L on the bench, so it ships as an experimental build. Same certificate caveat as the OpenPaper 7 (the vendor cloud certificate lives in a SPIFFS region the Tesserae layout overwrites; vendor support can re-provision it). Confirmed on real hardware running the tesserae-device-firmware build for this board; the panel path and GT911 touch are verified on glass (orientation by selftest corner taps, taps dispatched from a stay-awake panel with firmware 1.29.1); a tap waking the panel from deep sleep is the one path not yet exercised. Firmware 1.30.0 adds partial refresh (windowed two-tone patches in under a second against 1.2 s for a full 4-gray paint), so the panel advertises overlay: tap echo, device-drawn touch controls, live value slots and frame patches all apply, with quality repaints falling back to a full paint since the glass has no grayscale partial. Wire format is exactly 96000 bytes, 4 pixels per byte MSB first (bits 7-6 = leftmost pixel), 2-bit value 0b00 = black, 0b11 = white, linear 4-level gray; no header, no padding, no checksum.

**`native_w`/`native_h` are 480x800, matching the composition, not the controller's 800x480 scan.** These fields mean the row stride the *firmware* reads, and this firmware transposes on the device: it wants 120-byte portrait rows and rotates them itself. Declaring the controller's landscape scan here instead made the renderer rotate to landscape and pack 200-byte rows, which is still exactly 96000 bytes, so nothing errors and every frame painted as the image repeated sideways with the orientation wrong. Byte count alone does not validate this kind; the stride does.

Only the stride distinguishes it from `seeed_reterminal_e1001_gray`, which packs the same 96000 bytes at 800 wide because that firmware does not transpose.

`orientation` is `portrait`, pinned on hardware rather than inferred: a test frame of four grey bands with a white corner marker painted with the bands running top to bottom, black first, and the marker in the top-left, confirming both axes. Getting this wrong is a 180-degree error, so change it only against a real unit.

Supersedes `seeed_sticky` and `seeed_sticky_gray`, retired in v0.344.0. Those described the same hardware running CrossInk, were derived from the V01 schematic and Seeed's vendor demo rather than a validated unit, and declared a provisional `portrait_flipped` this board does not use. A kind is also an OTA lineage (release descriptors are signed with a `device_kind` and rejected on mismatch), so a second firmware would need its own kind again rather than a variant of this one. `migrate_retired_sticky_kinds` moves any instance still on the old ids.

`auto_select: false` because this SKU is indistinguishable on the wire from `xteink_x4_gray`: same protocol, same gamut, same 480x800 geometry, same 96000 bytes. A device running this firmware names its own kind at register and discover, so nothing is lost there, but relay pairing infers a SKU from the wire signature instead of reading a declared kind, and this id sorts ahead of `xteink_x4_gray` in that tie-break. Without this flag an Xteink X4 pairing over a relay would be relabelled a reTerminal Sticky.

touch_enabled.label: Touch input
touch_enabled.help: Wake on touch and dispatch taps/swipes against the dashboard's touch regions. Keeps the touch controller powered through deep sleep (a few mA continuous, or about 1 mA with Touch wake set to double tap or swipe), which reduces battery life; best on USB power.

touch_wake.label: Touch wake
touch_wake.help: How the touch controller waits through deep sleep. Any tap keeps it scanning, so the first touch wakes the panel, at a few mA all the time. Double tap or swipe parks it in its gesture mode (about 1 mA): a single first tap does nothing, a double tap or a swipe wakes the panel, and taps then work as usual while it is awake. Only applies while touch input is enabled; needs firmware 1.44.0 or later.

touch_linger_s.label: Touch linger
touch_linger_s.help: Seconds to stay awake after a touch interaction so follow-up taps skip the deep-sleep wake latency (boot + WiFi). 0 sleeps immediately. Only applies while touch input is enabled.

beep_enabled.label: Beep on interaction
beep_enabled.help: Sound the on-board buzzer the moment a touch or a button press registers, before the server is contacted. E-ink takes seconds to repaint, so without it there is no confirmation the panel heard you. Off by default: a panel that starts beeping unannounced is worse than a silent one.

beep_tone.label: Beep tone
beep_tone.help: Which sound to make. The server sends the actual notes, so these are editable without a firmware update. The buzzer is a passive piezo, loudest around 2 kHz.

beep_pattern.label: Custom tone
beep_pattern.help: Only used when the tone is set to Custom. Notes as frequency:milliseconds pairs, comma separated, e.g. 1800:30,2600:40. A frequency of 0 is a rest. Up to 8 notes, 200-8000 Hz, 1 second total.

beep_volume.label: Beep volume
beep_volume.help: Drive strength as a percentage. The piezo is loudest at 100 and audible but discreet around 30; 0 is silent, same as turning the beep off.

manifest.name: Seeed XIAO 7.5" ePaper Panel (C3, TRMNL BYOS)
manifest.description: Seeed's integrated XIAO 7.5 inch ePaper Panel (ESP32-C3) running the XIAO TRMNL firmware, so it speaks Tesserae's TRMNL BYOS endpoints; 4 greys on TRMNL firmware 1.6.0 and later, 1-bit below. Same hardware as xiao_epaper_panel_75_c3, the kind for the Tesserae-native firmware.
manifest.notes_md:
Confirmed on real hardware running the XIAO TRMNL firmware. The XIAO TRMNL firmware sends its MAC in the Id header (uppercase, colon-separated); Tesserae's BYOS layer matches case-insensitively, no extra configuration needed.

TRMNL firmware 1.6.0 and later decodes a 2-bit greyscale PNG and paints 4 shades on this panel; earlier builds cannot decode one. The firmware sends its version in the `FW-Version` header on every poll, so a device on this kind moves to `trmnl_png_gray4` by itself once it reports 1.6.0 or later, and back to the 1-bit `trmnl_png` if it reports an older build. A renderer picked on the device card stays put. The panel reports `gray_4` while on the grey renderer and `mono` on the 1-bit one. A unit that provisioned itself by MAC lands on the bare `trmnl_client` kind, which offers `trmnl_png_gray4` as a device-card pick but does not follow the firmware version, so the switch is automatic only for an instance created on this kind. The 2-bit path is UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE on this unit.

manifest.name: Seeed XIAO ePaper 7.5" (S3, mono)
manifest.description: Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 Plus driver board plus a 7.5 inch monochrome ePaper panel (800x480), sold as the TRMNL 7.5" (OG) DIY Kit. Not the integrated XIAO 7.5" ePaper Panel (C3), which is a separate product around the same glass, see xiao_epaper_panel_75_c3. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API and paints a raw 1-bpp mono buffer (48000 bytes) produced by the esp32_bw_bin renderer. Byte-identical wire contract to the Seeed reTerminal E1001; the two panels are cross-compatible on the frame side. Battery state is reported as unknown for now, sense pin not wired in the reference board.
manifest.notes_md:
Awaiting confirmed test on real hardware. Wire format is exactly 48000 bytes (800*480/8), MSB=leftmost pixel, bit-set=white, bit-clear=black; no header, no padding, no checksum. Frame is byte-identical to the seeed_reterminal_e1001 target, so validate cross-panel by pointing the same renderer output at both. Renderer keeps normal top-left orientation; the firmware handles any physical panel-side mirror itself.

**Colour depth.** Mono is the default. Firmware that advertises `"gamuts": ["mono", "gray_4"]` in its register and status bodies can also paint a 4-level grey frame from `esp32_gray2_bin`: exactly 96000 bytes (800*480/4), the same bytes as `seeed_reterminal_e1001_gray`, 4 px/byte MSB first, `0b00` black to `0b11` white. The firmware tells the two apart by byte length (48000 mono, 96000 grey), keeps the same kind, model and device id, and only firmware that advertises `gray_4` gets a grey frame, whatever the device card says. Older firmware omits the key and stays on mono. Pick the depth on the device card (Rendering, Colour depth). The grey path is UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE and needs a firmware build that advertises `gamuts`. Relay-paired panels do not advertise it and stay mono.

manifest.name: Seeed XIAO ePaper 7.5" (black/white/red)
manifest.description: Seeed XIAO ESP32-S3 driving a 7.5 inch black/white/red tri-colour ePaper panel (800x480). manifest.notes_md: Awaiting confirmed test on real hardware (firmware in progress). Wire format is exactly 96000 bytes (800*480/4), row-major from top-left, 4 pixels per byte MSB first (bits 7-6 = leftmost pixel); 2-bit value 0b00 = black, 0b01 = white, 0b10 = red, 0b11 reserved and never emitted by the server (firmware renders a stray 0b11 as white). No pre-rotation or mirroring; the firmware handles any panel-side transform. Same physical board as `xiao_epaper_75`; the server migrates a registered unit between the mono and BWR kinds automatically when its firmware re-registers or re-discovers declaring the other kind (same-protocol kind heal), keeping the device row, token, and history.

manifest.name: Seeed XIAO 7.5" ePaper Panel (C3)
manifest.description: Seeed's integrated XIAO 7.5 inch ePaper Panel, ESP32-C3 on-board (800x480 mono). Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API and paints a raw 1-bpp mono buffer (48000 bytes) produced by the esp32_bw_bin renderer; byte-identical wire contract to xiao_epaper_75 and the Seeed reTerminal E1001. Distinct from the XIAO ePaper 7.5" (S3) DIY kit, which is a different product around the same glass: the C3 unit has its own OTA lineage and its firmware image is not interchangeable. No battery telemetry (no divider to an ADC pin, so the panel reports no battery at all) and no user buttons beyond Boot and Reset.
manifest.notes_md:
Firmware support landed in tesserae-device-firmware v1.16.0; community bring-up in progress, not yet confirmed by the maintainer on real hardware. Wire format is exactly 48000 bytes (800*480/8), MSB=leftmost pixel, bit-set=white, bit-clear=black; no header, no padding, no checksum. Frame is byte-identical to the `xiao_epaper_75` and `seeed_reterminal_e1001` targets, so validate cross-panel by pointing the same renderer output at any of them. Default device ids look like `xiao_epaper_panel_75_<mac-suffix>` (model string `XIAO_ePaper_Panel_75`). OTA-capable; descriptors are signed for this kind id, so a `xiao_epaper_75` descriptor will be rejected by the firmware and vice versa.

**Not the same product as `xiao_epaper_75`.** That kind is the XIAO ePaper 7.5" (S3) DIY kit: a XIAO ESP32-S3 Plus driver board plus the same 7.5 inch glass, sold as the TRMNL 7.5" (OG) DIY Kit. This kind is the integrated panel with an ESP32-C3 on board. They pack identical frames but take different firmware images, so pick the one that matches the board you flashed. `seeed_xiao_75` is this same C3 hardware running TRMNL BYOS firmware instead of the Tesserae-native build.

**No battery reporting.** The C3 panel has no divider to any ADC pin, so the firmware reports no battery reading. Tesserae treats an absent `battery_pct` as "unknown" rather than "empty": the topbar indicator, the /devices/battery dashboard, and the low-battery frame overlay all skip a device with no `battery_pct`, so this panel simply carries no battery UI. Firmware must OMIT `battery_pct` from the heartbeat rather than sending `0`; a literal `battery_pct: 0` would read as a flat cell and paint the low-battery chip on every frame. Sending `battery_mv: 0` alone is harmless server-side, though it does publish a permanent 0 mV "Battery voltage" sensor when Home Assistant discovery is enabled, so omitting both fields is cleanest.

**No buttons.** Boot and Reset only, so there are no button-report mappings and no page-turn bindings for this kind. The protocol's `button_wake_s` config field is inherited from `esp32_bw_client` and has no effect here; leave it at 0. No Bluetooth setup path either, Wi-Fi provisioning only.

**Colour depth.** Mono is the default. Firmware that advertises `"gamuts": ["mono", "gray_4"]` in its register and status bodies can also paint a 4-level grey frame from `esp32_gray2_bin`: exactly 96000 bytes (800*480/4), the same bytes as `seeed_reterminal_e1001_gray`, 4 px/byte MSB first, `0b00` black to `0b11` white. The firmware tells the two apart by byte length (48000 mono, 96000 grey), keeps the same kind, model and device id, and only firmware that advertises `gray_4` gets a grey frame, whatever the device card says. Older firmware omits the key and stays on mono. Pick the depth on the device card (Rendering, Colour depth). The grey path is UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE and needs a firmware build that advertises `gamuts`. Relay-paired panels do not advertise it and stay mono.

manifest.name: Soldered Inkplate 10
manifest.description: 9.7 inch E Ink panel (1200x825, 16-level greyscale glass driven at the Inkplate library's 8 levels) on an ESP32-WROVER with Wi-Fi, battery charger, RTC, microSD, three capacitive touchpads and a wake button. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API from the tesserae.inkplate firmware and paints the esp32_gray_bin 4-bpp packed frame directly into its framebuffer. The server dithers to the 8 levels the firmware drives.

panel.name: 9.7 inch E Ink, 16-level greyscale driven at 8 levels (1200x825)

manifest.notes_md:
Verified on real hardware by the firmware author (partridgeworks/tesserae.inkplate), 2026-09. Inkplate 10 units have shipped with more than one 9.7 inch E Ink panel over the years; the firmware drives whichever is fitted through the Inkplate library, so no panel part number is pinned here.

Wire format is exactly 495000 bytes (1200*825/2), row-major from the top-left of the landscape framebuffer, high nibble = left pixel, 0x0 = black .. 0xF = white. The firmware halves each nibble to the panel's 8 grey levels and does a full refresh (about 1.6 s). The kind declares the `gray_8` gamut, so the server dithers against those 8 levels (k*255/7) and writes them as the nibbles 0, 2, 4, 6, 9, 11, 13, 15, which halve to 0..7; dithering against 16 levels would aim at greys the panel merges in pairs. The firmware reports `gray_16` at pairing (the depth of its frame); the server keeps this kind's `gray_8` for it, and instances created before 0.469.0 move onto `gray_8` at startup. Register the device with the rotation that matches its mount (the firmware sends 270 for portrait with the USB connector at the bottom); adjust in Settings -> Devices if it lands upside down. The same firmware also accepts esp32_bw_bin (1-bpp) and esp32_gray2_bin (2-bpp) frames, detected by byte count, so the stock esp32_bw_client kind works as a mono fallback when this catalog entry is not installed.

manifest.name: Soldered Inkplate 13SPECTRA
manifest.description: 13.3 inch E Ink Spectra 6 panel (1600x1200 landscape) on an ESP32-S3 with octal PSRAM, Wi-Fi, battery charger and microSD. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API from the inkplate-tesserae-driver firmware and paints the esp32_bin 4-bpp Spectra 6 frame into the Inkplate framebuffer.
manifest.notes_md:
Community firmware by [ripking/inkplate-tesserae-driver](https://github.com/ripking/inkplate-tesserae-driver); palette and orientation checked on real hardware by the author with the firmware's self-test build, and running dashboards since 2026-10. Full refresh takes about 20-30 s.

Wire format is exactly 960000 bytes (1600*1200/2), row-major from the top-left of the landscape frame, high nibble = left pixel. Nibbles are the Spectra 6 controller codes (0 black, 1 white, 2 yellow, 3 red, 5 blue, 6 green; 4 and 7 reserved), the same palette as the seeed_ee02 and waveshare_133e6 targets. The firmware turns the landscape frame onto the panel's portrait framebuffer itself; for a portrait or flipped mount, set the device's orientation in Settings -> Devices and the server turns the frame.

manifest.name: Soldered Inkplate 6COLOR
manifest.description: 5.85 inch 7-colour ACeP panel (600x448) on an ESP32 with Wi-Fi, battery charger, RTC and microSD. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API from the inkplate-tesserae-driver firmware and paints the esp32_bin 4-bpp palette-index frame straight into the Inkplate framebuffer.
manifest.notes_md:
Community firmware by [ripking/inkplate-tesserae-driver](https://github.com/ripking/inkplate-tesserae-driver), run on real hardware by the author for several months. Full refresh takes about 20-30 s.

Wire format is exactly 134400 bytes (600*448/2), row-major from the top-left, high nibble = left pixel. Nibbles follow the Inky 7-colour order (0 black, 1 white, 2 green, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 yellow, 6 orange), which matches the Inkplate library's `INKPLATE_*` colour constants one to one. Servers before 0.415.0 sent nibbles 2-5 in a different order (#298); firmware tuned against those servers needs its palette table made a pass-through. The firmware can also pair under the stock `esp32_client` kind with `gamut` `inky_7colour`, which produces the same frame.

manifest.name: TRMNL X
manifest.description: TRMNL X, 10.3 inch ePaper at 1872x1404 with 16 grey levels. Stock firmware speaks TRMNL BYOS and reports its model as `x`; Tesserae sends it a 4-bit greyscale PNG (trmnl_png_gray16), with the 1-bit trmnl_png still selectable on the device card.
manifest.notes_md:
Confirmed on real hardware running the stock TRMNL firmware. It auto-provisions on first poll; Tesserae provisions it on this kind and picks the native 1872x1404 panel from the Model header. Point the device's API URL at your Tesserae base URL and pair via the access token shown in Settings -> Devices.

The X paints 16 grey shades, and TRMNL documents a 4-bit greyscale PNG (colour type 0) for it, so this kind defaults to `trmnl_png_gray16` and sets `png_bit_depth: 4` in its `protocol_config`; the renderer then writes a true 4-bit PNG (other clients of that renderer, such as KOReader, keep the 8-bit encode). The 1-bit `trmnl_png` stays selectable on the device card, and the panel reports `mono` while it is picked. A TRMNL X provisioned before 0.469.0 sits on the bare `trmnl_client` kind with the 1-bit renderer; pick `trmnl_png_gray16` on its card, or re-provision it, to get the greys. The 4-bit PNG path is UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE.

manifest.name: Waveshare PhotoPainter 7.3"
manifest.description: 7.3 inch 6-colour Spectra E6 ePaper photo frame, ESP32-S3, battery-powered (800x480). Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API and paints a raw 4-bpp Spectra 6 buffer (192000 bytes) produced by the esp32_bin renderer. Same wire contract as the Seeed reTerminal E1002; the two panels are byte-compatible on the frame side. The PhotoPainter mounts its panel 180 deg in the case and the firmware rotates on-device, so the server renders in normal top-left orientation (no pre-rotate here).
manifest.notes_md: Confirmed on real hardware running tesserae-device-firmware. Palette nibbles align with the firmware's Spectra 6 constants byte-for-byte (black=0x0, white=0x1, yellow=0x2, red=0x3, blue=0x5, green=0x6; 0x4 and 0x7 reserved), and the buffer is byte-identical to the Seeed reTerminal E1002 output at 800x480: two pixels per byte, high nibble = LEFT (even column), low nibble = RIGHT (odd column), row-major, 400 bytes per row, top-left origin. Do not pre-rotate at render time even though the panel mounts 180 deg physically; the firmware rotates on-device.

manifest.name: Waveshare 4.2" B/W e-paper
manifest.description: 4.2 inch monochrome ePaper module, 400x300, driven by an ESP32 client. Frames are dithered server-side to 1-bpp and pushed over MQTT as a packed buffer.
manifest.notes_md: Awaiting confirmed test on real hardware. Pair with the tesserae-device-esp32-bw firmware.

manifest.name: Waveshare 10.85" e-Paper HAT+ (G) (ESP32-S3 Zero)
manifest.description: 10.85 inch four-colour (black/white/yellow/red) ePaper HAT+ (G) driven by a Waveshare ESP32-S3 Zero (ESP32-S3FH4R2, 4 MB flash, 2 MB PSRAM). 1360x480 landscape-native panel split across two 680-column controllers. Pair with the tesserae-device-firmware ESP-IDF build (env waveshare-1085g, boards/waveshare_1085g.h); the firmware bit-bangs the panel's SPI because the adapter needs a chip-select pulse per byte.
manifest.notes_md: Confirmed on real hardware running tesserae-device-firmware (community bring-up, firmware PR #31). Wire format is exactly 163200 bytes (1360*480*2/8): 2-bpp packed, four pixels per byte, MSB pair = leftmost pixel, palette indices 0=black, 1=white, 2=yellow, 3=red, row-major, 340 bytes per row, top-left origin. The firmware splits each row into two 170-byte halves for the left and right controllers, so the server packs one flat landscape frame with no stride padding. The ESP32-S3 Zero pin map in the firmware is a no-solder profile that differs from Waveshare's own ESP32-S3 demo wiring; follow boards/waveshare_1085g.h.

manifest.name: Waveshare 13.3" Spectra E6 (ESP32-S3)
manifest.description: 13.3 inch 6-colour Spectra E6 ePaper module driven by an ESP32-S3-WROOM-2-N32R16V. 1200x1600 portrait-native panel, dual-SPI controller (left/right halves), single-cell Li-Po battery via onboard ETA6098 charger. Frames are packed server-side to 4-bpp Spectra E6 (960000 bytes) and delivered over Tesserae's v1 REST device API. manifest.notes_md: Confirmed on real hardware running tesserae-device-firmware. Pair with `tesserae-device-firmware` (ESP-IDF); the board header at `boards/waveshare_133e6.h` supplies the pin map + palette nibble constants (which match Tesserae's WAVESHARE_E6 nibble mapping byte-for-byte). Default sleep interval is 15 minutes; hash-skip wakes cost roughly 0.13 mAh, render wakes roughly 0.75 mAh.

manifest.name: Waveshare 7.3" e-Paper (F) on an ESP32-S3
manifest.description: Waveshare's 7.3 inch 7-colour ACeP panel (800x480, AC073TC1A) wired to an ESP32-S3 with octal PSRAM. Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API and paints a 4-bpp palette-index frame (192000 bytes) in the panel's own colour order, so the firmware sends it to the controller unchanged.
manifest.notes_md:
**UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE.** Firmware support is the `waveshare-epaper-73f` build in tesserae-device-firmware; flash `waveshare-epaper-73f-selftest` first and check the seven colour bands (black, white, yellow, red, blue, green, orange, top to bottom).

Wire format is exactly 192000 bytes (800*480/2), row-major from the top-left, high nibble = left pixel. Nibbles follow the ACeP controller's order (0 black, 1 white, 2 green, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 yellow, 6 orange), the same packing as the Inkplate 6COLOR and the original Inky Frame 7.3". This is the older 7-colour glass; Waveshare's newer 7.3 inch (E) panel is Spectra 6 and is a different kind (the PhotoPainter uses it).

**Pins.** There is no single board for this panel, so the build carries a default pin map for an ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1 (SCLK 12, MOSI 11, CS 10, DC 9, RST 8, BUSY 7) and each pin can be overridden at build time. The build targets a 16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM module (N16R8).

No battery reporting and no buttons.

manifest.name: Waveshare E-Paper ESP32 Driver Board + 7.5" B/W
manifest.description: Waveshare's universal E-Paper ESP32 Driver Board (classic ESP32-WROOM-32, 4 MB flash, no PSRAM) carrying a 7.5 inch monochrome panel (7.5inch e-Paper V2, 800x480). Speaks Tesserae's v1 REST device API and paints a raw 1-bpp mono buffer (48000 bytes) produced by the esp32_bw_bin renderer; byte-identical wire contract to the Seeed reTerminal E1001 and the XIAO 7.5 inch boards. Distinct kind because the classic-ESP32 firmware image has its own OTA lineage. No battery telemetry (the board has no divider to an ADC pin) and no user buttons beyond EN and BOOT.
manifest.notes_md:
Firmware support is in tesserae-device-firmware from v1.32.0 as the `waveshare-esp32-driver-75` build; community bring-up, not yet confirmed on real hardware. Wire format is exactly 48000 bytes (800*480/8), MSB=leftmost pixel, bit-set=white, bit-clear=black; no header, no padding, no checksum. Frame is byte-identical to the `xiao_epaper_75`, `xiao_epaper_panel_75_c3` and `seeed_reterminal_e1001` targets. Default device ids look like `waveshare_esp32_driver_75_<mac-suffix>` (model string `Waveshare_ESP32_Driver_75`). OTA-capable; descriptors are signed for this kind id.

**Board switches.** Waveshare's wiki says DIP switch 1 (Display Config) must sit at the 0.47R "B" position for the 7.5 inch panel; the 3R "A" position is for the small panels and gives a faint or blank image. Switch 2 powers the USB-UART bridge and must be ON to flash or to see the serial console.

**Panel fit.** The firmware drives the 7.5 inch V2 (UC8179, 800x480). Waveshare's older 7.5 inch V1 (640x384) and the tri-colour (B) and (C) panels are not this kind.

**No battery reporting.** The board's 5V pin accepts 3.6-5.5 V so it can run from a cell, but nothing on the board measures it, so the firmware omits `battery_pct` and the server shows no battery UI for this kind.

**No buttons.** EN and BOOT only, so no button-report mappings, no page-turn bindings and no Bluetooth setup path; Wi-Fi provisioning is the captive portal.

**Colour depth.** Mono is the default. Firmware that advertises `"gamuts": ["mono", "gray_4"]` in its register and status bodies can also paint a 4-level grey frame from `esp32_gray2_bin`: exactly 96000 bytes (800*480/4), the same bytes as `seeed_reterminal_e1001_gray`, 4 px/byte MSB first, `0b00` black to `0b11` white. The firmware tells the two apart by byte length (48000 mono, 96000 grey), keeps the same kind, model and device id, and only firmware that advertises `gray_4` gets a grey frame, whatever the device card says. Older firmware omits the key and stays on mono. Pick the depth on the device card (Rendering, Colour depth). The grey path is UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE and needs a firmware build that advertises `gamuts`. Relay-paired panels do not advertise it and stay mono.

manifest.name: Xteink X3
manifest.description: Monochrome ePaper e-reader, ESP32-C3, 792x528 panel mounted portrait (528x792 presentation). Sibling of the Xteink X4 sharing the same firmware binary and the same Tesserae client path, but with a larger panel and a different controller family (UC8253, or UC8279d on later production runs). Server-side pack via esp32_bw_bin produces a raw 1-bpp mono buffer of 52272 bytes.
manifest.notes_md:
Wire format is exactly 52272 bytes (792*528/8), MSB=leftmost pixel, bit-set=white, bit-clear=black; no header, no padding, no checksum. 792 is a multiple of 8, so the packer needs no row padding.

The panel block is confirmed on real hardware via the grayscale sibling `xteink_x3_gray`, which shares it: a dashboard composed at 528x792 and packed at the 792x528 native stride renders upright on an X3, so both the geometry and `portrait_flipped` are measured rather than inherited from the X4.

The 1-bpp path itself has not been exercised on an X3, only the 2-bpp one. It is the same frame at half the size through `esp32_bw_bin`, which is confirmed on the X4, so the remaining risk is small.

Later X3 production runs ship a UC8279d controller instead of the UC8253. The firmware detects which at boot and both take the same buffer; only the UC8279d has been tested.

manifest.name: Xteink X3 (4-level grayscale)
manifest.description: Xteink X3 driven in its 4-level grayscale mode rather than pure 1-bit mono. Same 792x528 panel mounted portrait (528x792 presentation) and the same CrossInk sleep-screen client as xteink_x3, but the server packs a 2-bpp buffer (104544 bytes) via esp32_gray2_bin and the firmware composites it as a base frame plus two grayscale planes. Pick this over xteink_x3 when the dashboard has photos or shading; stay on xteink_x3 for text and line art, where the extra levels buy little and the frame is half the size.
manifest.notes_md:
Confirmed on real hardware running CrossInk with Tesserae client support: a 4-level grayscale dashboard renders upright in portrait on an Xteink X3.

Wire format is exactly 104544 bytes (792*528/4), 4 px/byte, MSB-first, `0b00` black to `0b11` white, linear. That packing matches CrossInk's own 2-bpp bitmap reader, so the firmware expands the frame straight into its `GRAYSCALE_LSB` / `GRAYSCALE_MSB` planes with no decode. The X3 additionally needs the OEM preconditioning settle pass between the base frame and the planes, which the firmware issues unconditionally (it is a no-op on the X4).

Worth noting for anyone extending `esp32_gray2_bin`: this renderer is described as targeting UC8179-class silicon, and the X3 is UC8253 / UC8279d. It works there too. Only the UC8279d production run has been exercised so far.

`portrait_flipped` is confirmed rather than inherited: the X3 has a different controller family from the X4 but the same framebuffer scan origin, so the same 180-degree correction applies.

manifest.name: Xteink X4
manifest.description: 4.26 inch monochrome ePaper e-reader, ESP32-C3, 800x480 panel mounted portrait (480x800 presentation). Two firmware paths speak Tesserae's v1 REST device API: CrossInk with Tesserae client support, which paints the dashboard as the reader's sleep screen on an explicit sleep transition (the radio never comes up on a timer), and the native Tesserae device firmware (`xteink-x4`), which polls on the normal deep-sleep cadence with the power button advancing the rotation. Server-side pack via esp32_bw_bin produces a raw 1-bpp mono buffer (48000 bytes) painted with no on-device decode; both firmwares consume identical bytes.
manifest.notes_md:
Confirmed on real hardware (GDEQ0426T82 / SSD1677) on both firmware paths: CrossInk 1.4.0 with Tesserae client support, and the native Tesserae device firmware (tesserae-device-firmware env `xteink-x4`).

Wire format is exactly 48000 bytes (800*480/8), MSB=leftmost pixel, bit-set=white, bit-clear=black; no header, no padding, no checksum, identical to seeed_reterminal_e1001 and xiao_epaper_75.

Orientation is the ordinary presentational setting and the two firmwares agree on it: the same registration (`portrait_flipped`, this entry's default) has painted upright on both CrossInk and the native firmware on the same unit, so no per-firmware value is needed. Pick the orientation matching the physical mounting, as on any panel. Historical diagnosis note: plain `portrait` painted 180 degrees out (readable, rotated, no mirror), first isolated by registering the unit against the landscape `xiao_epaper_75` kind, hence the flipped default for a reader stood upright.

Xteink shipped a second panel revision mid-production (SSD1677 -> UC8179; later runs also UC8279). CrossInk detects the controller at boot and both revisions consume the same buffer, so no separate SKU is needed there. The native Tesserae firmware is an SSD1677-only build: a UC8179/UC8279 unit will not refresh on it at all and needs a firmware target of its own.

See `xteink_x4_gray` for the 4-level grayscale kind CrossInk uses. The native Tesserae firmware stays on this kind for both depths (see Colour depth below).

**Colour depth.** Mono is the default. Firmware that advertises `"gamuts": ["mono", "gray_4"]` in its register and status bodies can also paint a 4-level grey frame from `esp32_gray2_bin`: exactly 96000 bytes (800*480/4) at the 800x480 native stride, the exact frame `xteink_x4_gray` gets, 4 px/byte MSB first, `0b00` black to `0b11` white. The firmware tells the two apart by byte length (48000 mono, 96000 grey), keeps the same kind, model and device id, and only firmware that advertises `gray_4` gets a grey frame, whatever the device card says. Older firmware omits the key and stays on mono. Pick the depth on the device card (Rendering, Colour depth). The grey path is UNVERIFIED ON HARDWARE and needs a firmware build that advertises `gamuts`. Relay-paired panels do not advertise it and stay mono.

manifest.name: Xteink X4 (4-level grayscale)
manifest.description: Xteink X4 driven in its 4-level grayscale mode rather than pure 1-bit mono. Same 800x480 panel mounted portrait (480x800 presentation) and the same CrossInk sleep-screen client as xteink_x4, but the server packs a 2-bpp buffer (96000 bytes) via esp32_gray2_bin and the firmware composites it as a base frame plus two grayscale planes. Pick this over xteink_x4 when the dashboard has photos or shading; stay on xteink_x4 for text and line art, where the extra levels buy little and the frame is half the size.
manifest.notes_md:
Confirmed on real hardware (GDEQ0426T82 / SSD1677) running CrossInk with Tesserae client support: a 4-level grayscale dashboard renders upright in portrait with distinct grey levels.

Grayscale sibling of `xteink_x4`, mirroring the `seeed_reterminal_e1001_gray` pattern: same `esp32_bw_client` protocol and panel block as the mono entry, with the renderer overridden to `esp32_gray2_bin`.

Wire format is exactly 96000 bytes (800*480/4), 4 px/byte, MSB-first, `0b00` black to `0b11` white, linear. That packing and those level semantics match CrossInk's own 2-bpp bitmap reader byte for byte, so the firmware expands the frame straight into its `GRAYSCALE_LSB` / `GRAYSCALE_MSB` planes with no decode: LSB set where the level is 1, MSB set where it is 1 or 2, and the base frame white only where the level is 3.

The X4's newer panel revision (SSD1677 -> UC8179) is the UC81xx-class silicon this renderer targets; the firmware detects the controller at boot and both revisions take the same buffer.

Costs relative to `xteink_x4`: double the download per refresh, and three panel passes instead of one (base frame plus two planes), so a noticeably longer sleep-entry paint on a battery shared with an e-reader. Choose the mono entry for text and line art, this one for photos and shading.

manifest.name: Xteink X4 Pro
manifest.description: 4.2 inch monochrome ePaper e-reader, ESP32-S3 sibling of the X4 with capacitive touch and a warm/cool frontlight. Same 800x480 SSD1677 panel mounted portrait (480x800 presentation) and the same 48000-byte 1-bpp wire format, so the frame is byte-identical to the xteink_x4 target.
manifest.notes_md:
Panel block confirmed on real hardware via the grayscale sibling `xteink_x4_pro_gray`, which shares it: a dashboard composed at 480x800 and packed at the 800x480 native stride renders upright on an X4 Pro running CrossInk, so both the geometry and `portrait_flipped` are measured rather than inherited from the X4.

The 1-bpp path itself has not been exercised on an X4 Pro, only the 2-bpp one. It is the same frame at half the size through `esp32_bw_bin`, which is confirmed on the X4 (same SSD1677 controller, 800x480, 48000 bytes), so the remaining risk is small. The board profile differs from the X4 only in MCU (ESP32-S3), touch, frontlight and a PSRAM-backed framebuffer.

See `xteink_x4_pro_gray` for the 4-level grayscale variant of the same panel; the released CrossInk `x4-pro` build ships with grayscale on and announces that id.

manifest.name: ZecTrix NOTE4C Devkit
manifest.description: Battery-powered 400x300 four-colour BWRY (black/white/red/yellow) e-paper devkit. Community firmware by varanu5 speaks Tesserae's REST device API and Cloud relay, and paints frames the esp32_bin renderer packs to 2-bpp BWRY. Shares the PicPak wire protocol.
manifest.notes_md: Community firmware by [varanu5](https://github.com/varanu5/zectrix-note4c-devkit-tesserae-client), confirmed on real hardware over REST and Cloud relay. For the four-colour NOTE4C only, not the grayscale NOTE4. The firmware enforces a 30 second minimum sleep interval.

manifest.name: Bloomin8 Canvas
manifest.description: Bloomin8 Canvas colour e-paper frame using its Schedule Pull API. Point the Canvas's upstream URL at <tesserae>/api/bloomin8 with the access token shown on the device card; it wakes on schedule, calls /eink_pull for the latest frame as a baseline JPEG, paints it, and sleeps until the next wake Tesserae hands back. Wakes follow the page's schedule within the configured interval. The Canvas dithers for its own panel, so the frame is sent full colour.

sleep_interval_s.label: Wake interval
sleep_interval_s.help: The longest the Canvas sleeps between pulls. A scheduled page change pulls the wake earlier so the new frame lands on time. Manual Send and Home Assistant triggers have no schedule to follow, so this is how long they can take to show. Bloomin8 asks for at least a minute between wakes.

manifest.name: CircuitPython client (generic)
manifest.description: Generic CircuitPython client kind for boards driving an e-paper panel from a Pico W / Pico 2 W / Feather / similar microcontroller. Serves the composition already quantised to the panel's palette, as an indexed PNG (default) or an uncompressed indexed BMP, either of which adafruit_imageload decodes directly. Declare format:'bmp' on discover for memory-constrained boards (Pico W class), where CircuitPython's one-shot zlib.decompress can't fit a PNG's decode buffer; the BMP needs no zlib. Pairing follows the v1 REST discover-and-approve flow (POST /api/v1/device/discover with the board's MAC); steady state polls GET /api/v1/device/<id>/frame and POSTs heartbeats to /status. The kind is deliberately broad: a maintainer's own circuitpython_<board> kind (e.g. circuitpython_pico_w_inky) is welcome and stays compatible, this entry is the catch-all so boards without a tighter manifest still register cleanly.

sleep_interval_s.label: Sleep interval
sleep_interval_s.help: How long the client sleeps between /frame polls. Tesserae echoes the value back in the /status response as next_poll_s so the firmware doesn't need its own persistent setting.

manifest.name: CrossPoint e-reader (sleep screen)
manifest.description: CrossPoint e-readers painting a Tesserae dashboard as their sleep screen, over the LAN with no cloud component. The reader draws the image twice, through its GRAYSCALE_LSB and GRAYSCALE_MSB planes, quantising each pixel to 0-3, so the panel is a four-level greyscale ramp and the composition is rendered to the gray_4 gamut rather than to mono. Registering as a generic CircuitPython client left the panel on a mono default and threw those levels away server-side, before the file was written. Pairing is the v1 REST flow: POST /api/v1/device/discover with the reader's derived MAC (locally administered 02: range, so it cannot collide with a real NIC), or the 6-digit code fallback via /register. Steady state is a heartbeat to /status on book close, and a pull of GET /api/v1/device/<id>/frame.bmp for the image itself, which the reader downloads in one request with no redirects.

sleep_interval_s.label: Refresh interval
sleep_interval_s.help: How often the server expects the reader back. The reader pulls its sleep screen when the book closes rather than on a timer, so this mainly decides how long it can be silent before the Devices card calls it stale.

manifest.name: ESP32 BW client
manifest.description: Battery-powered ESP32 firmware for mono B/W e-paper panels (e.g. Waveshare 4.2" 400x300). Subscribes to tesserae/esp32/frame/bin (retained), paints the panel via SPI, then deep-sleeps. Publishes battery / RSSI / IP heartbeats on wake; reads its sleep-interval config from the broker.

button_wake_s.label: Button wake window
button_wake_s.help: After a button press changes the page, stay awake this many seconds to catch rapid repeat presses before deep-sleeping, so scrolling several pages doesn't pay a fresh wake and Wi-Fi cycle per press. 0 sleeps immediately (best battery). Applies only to button wakes, not scheduled refreshes or rotation.

always_on.label: Stay awake
always_on.help: Skip deep sleep entirely and poll on the awake interval below. A Send, a schedule or a touch then lands within seconds instead of on the next wake. Draws Wi-Fi power continuously, so this is for mains-powered panels only; the option is offered only to firmware that reports it can stay awake.

awake_poll_s.label: Awake poll interval
awake_poll_s.help: How often to re-check for a new frame while staying awake. Ignored unless Stay awake is on. Unchanged content answers 304 without a panel refresh, so a short interval costs one small request rather than an e-paper repaint.

manifest.name: ESP32 client
manifest.description: Battery-powered ESP32 firmware that subscribes to tesserae/esp32/frame/bin (retained), paints the panel via SPI, and goes back to deep sleep. Publishes battery / RSSI / IP heartbeats on wake; reads its sleep-interval config from the broker.

button_wake_s.help: After a button press changes the page, stay awake this many seconds to catch rapid repeat presses before deep-sleeping, so scrolling several pages doesn't pay a fresh wake and Wi-Fi cycle per press. 0 sleeps immediately (best battery). Draws Wi-Fi power continuously, so this is for mains-powered panels only; the option is offered only to firmware that reports it can stay awake.

manifest.name: KOReader e-reader
manifest.description: Jailbroken Kindle, Kobo, and other e-readers running KOReader with the Tesserae plugin (dmellok/tesserae-koreader). The plugin pairs with a claim code, polls GET /api/v1/device/<id>/frame on the configured cadence, decodes the packed 16-level greyscale frame on the device, and sleeps between refreshes. A colour reader (E Ink Kaleido 3: Kobo Libra Colour, Clara Colour) pairs with gamut kaleido3 and is served a colour PNG instead. The e-reader reports its own screen size at pairing, so one kind covers every model.

sleep_interval_s.label: Refresh interval
sleep_interval_s.help: How long the e-reader sleeps between frame fetches. Tesserae echoes it back on every status poll as next_poll_s. Shorter intervals cost battery on readers that sleep between refreshes; on readers kept awake they only cost a small request when nothing changed.

manifest.name: OpenDisplay tag
manifest.description: An OpenDisplay BLE e-paper tag, driven by the tesserae-opendisplay bridge. Tesserae renders a full-colour PNG; the bridge polls the frame over REST and pushes it to the tag over Bluetooth LE with the py-opendisplay SDK, which dithers for whatever panel the tag advertises. One bridge drives many tags. The panel dimensions here are a placeholder: the bridge registers each tag with its real advertised size, so the composition renders at the correct aspect. REST-polled, honours sleep_interval_s (echoed back as next_poll_s).

panel.name: OpenDisplay tag (placeholder; bridge sets the real size)

sleep_interval_s.label: Sleep interval
sleep_interval_s.help: How long the bridge sleeps between frame polls for this tag. BLE image pushes are slow, and e-paper updates infrequently, so a longer interval is usually right. Custom value is in seconds.

manifest.name: OpenDisplay tag (via Home Assistant)
manifest.description: An OpenDisplay BLE e-paper tag driven through Home Assistant. Tesserae renders a full-colour PNG, writes it into HA's media folder, and calls the opendisplay.upload_image action; HA's OpenDisplay integration pushes it to the tag over Bluetooth LE and dithers for the panel. No separate bridge or BLE hardware on the Tesserae host. Set the tag's HA device id below. Best when Tesserae runs as the Home Assistant add-on (shared /media). Requires the Home Assistant Core plugin.

ha_device_id.label: HA device
ha_device_id.help: Pick your tag from Home Assistant's OpenDisplay devices; Tesserae stores its device id and, when the model reports a resolution, fills the panel size. If Home Assistant isn't reachable, type the device id by hand (its internal hex id, e.g. 4ab9c7f0e2…, not the tag's own name/serial). Requires the Home Assistant Core plugin.

rotate.label: Rotation
rotate.help: Rotation applied by the HA upload action, if the tag's mounting needs it.

manifest.name: Pi BIN client
manifest.description: Raspberry-Pi-side client that consumes the 4-bpp .bin frame. Subscribes to tesserae/pi_bin/frame/bin; publishes a heartbeat with idle/rendering state and the last paint timestamp. REST-polled instances also honour sleep_interval_s — Tesserae echoes the configured cadence back in the /api/v1/device/<id>/status response as next_poll_s so the client knows when to wake.

sleep_interval_s.label: Sleep interval
sleep_interval_s.help: How long the client sleeps between frame fetches when polling via REST. MQTT-driven instances ignore this value (they wake on retained-frame publishes). Custom value is in seconds.

manifest.name: Pi PNG client
manifest.description: Raspberry-Pi-side client that consumes the PNG frame. Subscribes to tesserae/pi_png/frame/png; publishes a heartbeat with idle/rendering state and the last paint timestamp. REST-polled instances also honour sleep_interval_s — Tesserae echoes the configured cadence back in the /api/v1/device/<id>/status response as next_poll_s so the client knows when to wake.

sleep_interval_s.label: Sleep interval
sleep_interval_s.help: How long the client sleeps between frame fetches when polling via REST. MQTT-driven instances ignore this value (they wake on retained-frame publishes). Custom value is in seconds.

manifest.name: Pico BIN client
manifest.description: Battery-powered Pico Plus 2 firmware (RP2350) driving a Pimoroni Inky-style Spectra 6 panel over SPI. Subscribes to tesserae/pico_bin/frame/bin (retained), wakes on sleep_interval_s, fetches the current .bin frame, paints, publishes a heartbeat with battery / RSSI / IP, then goes back to deep sleep. Landscape-native packing (consumes the pi_bin-style buffer); the firmware does the on-device 90 deg rotate + column-600 dual-controller split.

manifest.name: PicPak client
manifest.description: Battery-powered PicPak 4.2" 4-colour BWRY e-paper frame. Wakes on a timer, pulls the current frame over REST (or MQTT), paints the 400x300 panel via SPI, publishes a battery / RSSI heartbeat, and deep-sleeps. Reads its sleep-interval config from the server. Firmware: https://github.com/varanu5/picpak-tesserae-client

sleep_interval_s.label: Sleep interval
sleep_interval_s.help: How long the frame sleeps between fetches. Longer intervals extend battery life; typical dashboards use 15 to 60 minutes. Custom value is in seconds.

manifest.name: TRMNL client
manifest.description: HTTP-polled e-paper client compatible with the TRMNL BYOS protocol. Devices (jailbroken Kindles running the KOReader trmnl-display plugin, TRMNL devices, anything that speaks the protocol) poll GET /api/display on a fixed cadence and paint the latest frame. Identity is the access_token the user generates in Tesserae and pastes into the client config, no MAC, no MQTT, no pairing flow.

refresh_rate_s.label: Refresh rate
refresh_rate_s.help: How often the client polls /api/display for a new frame. The server echoes this back in the response so the client honours it (though some clients keep their own poll rate).

unified_platformio:
; PlatformIO Project Configuration File -- tesserae-device-firmware
;
; Multi-target Tesserae e-paper firmware: one codebase, one [env:...] per
; device. Each env selects a board (pin map + panel geometry + MCU tier +
; panel driver) via a -DTESSERAE_BOARD_* flag that boards/board.h dispatches
; on. The panel driver itself is bound at build time in src/panel/registry.c.
;
; Shared knobs live in [env] and are inherited by every target.

[env]
; Pinned to the pioarduino platform fork (ESP-IDF 5.5, ships the
; esp32-s3-devkitc1-n16r8 variant). The official registry "espressif32" does
; NOT carry that board, so this must be an explicit URL for reproducible CI.
platform = https://github.com/pioarduino/platform-espressif32/releases/download/55.03.37/platform-espressif32.zip
framework = espidf
monitor_speed = 115200
monitor_filters = esp32_exception_decoder, direct
; Ed25519 verification for signed OTA manifests. Pin the exact upstream commit
; behind Monocypher 4.0.3 so a moved tag cannot silently change the crypto code.
lib_deps =
    https://github.com/LoupVaillant/Monocypher.git#ab2b16dd619ad5f6979a4fbe69cfa324a6fcc35f
; sdkconfig.defaults at the project root is picked up automatically by the
; ESP-IDF integration; no extra path needed here.

; -----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Phase 0 target -- Waveshare ESP32-S3-ePaper-13.3E6
;   - Module: ESP32-S3-WROOM-2-N32R16V (32 MB flash, 16 MB octal PSRAM)
;   - Panel:  13.3" 1200x1600 6-color Spectra E6, dual-controller (CS_M/CS_S)
;   - Driver family A: spectra6_spi_dual
;
; Built against the n16r8 PlatformIO variant (16 MB flash, 8 MB octal PSRAM).
; That fits comfortably inside the real module's larger flash/PSRAM; if you
; later want OTA + dual app slots, bump board_build.flash_size to 32MB and
; widen the factory partition in partitions.csv.
; -----------------------------------------------------------------------
[env:waveshare-133e6]
board = esp32-s3-devkitc1-n16r8
board_build.cmake_extra_args = -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.ota.defaults;sdkconfig.coredump.defaults"

; FW_VERSION (reported in the status heartbeat) is injected by CI as an
; auto-incrementing 0.0.<build> string -- see .github/workflows/firmware.yml.
; Local builds have no flag and fall back to "0.0.0-dev" (include/app_config.h).
build_flags =
    -DTESSERAE_BOARD_WAVESHARE_133E6
    -DTESSERAE_OTA_CAPABILITY_ENABLED=1

board_build.partitions = partitions_ota.csv
board_build.flash_size = 16MB

; -----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Waveshare ESP32-S3-Zero + 10.85-inch e-Paper G
;   - Module: ESP32-S3FH4R2 (4 MB flash, 2 MB embedded Quad PSRAM)
;   - Panel:  1360x480 B/W/Y/R, dual 680px controller
;   - Driver: waveshare_1085g_dual (software SPI; no partial refresh)
;
; The PSRAM holds the 163200-byte full frame alongside Wi-Fi/TLS allocations.
; The board header uses the verified no-solder S3 Zero GPIO profile, rather
; than Waveshare's separate ESP32-S3 reference-board pin map.
; -----------------------------------------------------------------------
[env:waveshare-1085g]
board = esp32-s3-devkitc-1
board_build.cmake_extra_args = -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.s3-zero.defaults;sdkconfig.ota.defaults"

build_flags =
    -DTESSERAE_BOARD_WAVESHARE_1085G
    -DTESSERAE_OTA_CAPABILITY_ENABLED=1
board_build.partitions = partitions_4m_ota.csv
board_build.flash_size = 4MB
board_upload.flash_size = 4MB

; Driver-only bring-up (four colour bars, no networking) -- flash this first.
[env:waveshare-1085g-selftest]
extends = env:waveshare-1085g
build_flags =
    ${env:waveshare-1085g.build_flags}
    -DEPD_SELFTEST

; -----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Phase 1 target -- Seeed reTerminal E1004
;   - MCU:   XIAO ESP32-S3 class (ESP32-S3 + PSRAM)
;   - Panel: 13.3" T133A01, dual-chip Spectra-6, 1200x1600
;   - Driver: spectra6_t133a01_dual (Family A variant; NOT the 13.3E6 blobs)
;
; Built against the same n16r8 S3+octal-PSRAM tier stand-in as the base (our
; pins come from boards/seeed_reterminal_e1004.h, not the PlatformIO board).
; Hardware inspection on a production E1004 found a 32 MB flash chip. This env
; therefore has an E1004-only A/B layout with two 4 MB OTA slots. Its explicit
; offsets keep the existing NVS partition at 0x9000 so a one-time USB migration
; can preserve WiFi credentials and device registration.
;
; The existing E1004 board/panel path is hardware-proven. The A/B migration was
; verified on a production unit with NVS preserved; rollback fault tests remain.
; -----------------------------------------------------------------------
[env:seeed-reterminal-e1004]
board = esp32-s3-devkitc1-n16r8
board_build.cmake_extra_args = -DSDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.ble.defaults;sdkconfig.e1004-ota.defaults;sdkconfig.coredump.defaults"

build_flags =
    -DTESSERAE_BOARD_SEEED_E1004
    -DTESSERAE_OTA_CAPABILITY_ENABLED=1

board_build.partitions = partitions_e1004_ota.csv
board_build.flash_size = 32MB
board_upload.flash_size = 32MB

; Driver-only bring-up build for the E1004: on boot, init the panel and paint
; the 6 colour bars, then halt -- no WiFi/MQTT. Flash this first to validate
; the (unverified) T133A01 driver in isolation before the full firmware.
[env:seeed-reterminal-e1004-selftest]
extends = env:seeed-reterminal-e1004
build_flags =
    ${env:seeed-reterminal-e1004.build_flags}
    -DEPD_SELFTEST

; -----------------------------------------------------------------------
; Seeed reTerminal E1002 -- single-controller Spectra-6, 800x480 (Family B)
;   - Driver: spectra6_spi_single (ESP-IDF Spectra-6 update path,
;     confirmed working on real E1002 hardware).
; Same S3 + octal-PSRAM tier stand-in; pins come from the board header.
; -----------------------------------------------------------------------
[env:seeed-reterminal-e1002]
board = esp32-s3-devkitc1-n16r8
board_build.cmake_extra_args = -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.ble.defaults;sdkconfig.ota.defaults;sdkconfig.coredump.defaults"

build_flags =
    -DTESSERAE_BOARD_SEEED_E1002
    -DTESSERAE_OTA_CAPABILITY_ENABLED=1

; it; the offer does not depend on the comparison going the way you expect.

; the parent's build_flags, which is the whole point) and reports a sentinel

; must stay that way. It shares TESSERAE_DEVICE_KIND with the parent env, and
; release.yml stages each target's signing input as "<kind>.app.bin" into one
; directory -- so shipping both would have them overwrite each other, and the
; E1003 fleet could be handed a signed image with OTA compiled out. Adding a
; kind of its own would need a server catalog entry, which is far more than a
; bench build deserves. Keep it out of the matrices instead.
; -----------------------------------------------------------------------

extends = env:seeed-reterminal-e1003
build_flags =
    -DTESSERAE_BOARD_SEEED_E1003
    -DT3_HAVE_ICON_FONT
